text:
alex: Heads-up: planned KV-cache prefill + controlled traffic-shaping experiment tomorrow 2026-06-04 02:00 UTC (45m). Goal is to validate warmup hit-rate improvements and measure downstream p99 impact before the quantized rollout. SLOs: we will temporarily relax the generation p99 latency target from 120ms -> 220ms for the affected routes during the window. This is an internal SLO adjustment only, not a customer-visible SLA change.

mina: which routes/tenants are in scope?

alex: scope: /v1/generate (all tiers) but traffic will be steered to a canary pool (~10% traffic) in region-usw1 and region-eu1. No dedicated-customer reserved capacity will be affected. Tenants: internal test traffic + opt-in customers on the canary list (posted in #product).

jamal: oncall acked. I'll be on watch and idle to roll back if alerts trigger.

olivia: any customer comms? legal/ops signoff?

alex: not external. We've cleared compliance review; PMs for opt-in customers have been notified. If anything looks off we will abort and restore normal routing.

rohit: share the monitoring queries & runbook pls.

alex: pasted runbook snippet below and the PromQL we’ll use. If p50/p95/p99 deviate beyond thresholds or error_rate > 0.5% for 3m, escalate to pagers.

alex: ```Runbook (short):
1) watch dashboards: https://dash.board/redwood/kvcache-prefill (watch latency by route + canary pool)
2) if p99(gen) > 300ms AND error_rate > 0.5% -> rollback routing: `rdctl routing set /v1/generate default`
3) if memory pressure on GPU nodes > 85% -> throttle prefill via feature flag: `feature-flag set kvcache_prefill=false`
4) post-mortem tags: incident:type=experiment, impact:iffailed
```

alex: PromQL sample we'll attach to the dashboard:
```promql
avg_over_time(latency_ms_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])
rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status!~"2.."}[3m]) * 100
```

sre-bot: Reminder scheduled: kvcache prefill experiment starts in 10m (2755551234 -> 2755551834). :bell:

mina: will prefill cause a spike in egress or write IO? need to inform infra team about disk bursts.

alex: prefill is read-heavy on model kv-store and some memcopy to GPU; we expect transient network/RAM pressure on canary nodes only. infra aware and will throttle if needed.

jamal: setting a temporary quiet window for noisy non-prod jobs around the experiment.

rohit: adding a synthetic request load generator to the canary pool to stabilize seq-length distribution. Command I ran earlier: ```./stressgen --route /v1/generate --qps 50 --seq 1024 --duration 1800s```

olivia: thanks. Product will watch metrics and jump in if opt-in customers see anomalies.

deploy-bot: deploy started: kvcache-prefill-v2 -> canary-pool (deploy id d-99234). Logs: https://ci/redwood/d-99234

jamal: noted deploy. I’ll monitor the canary health checks and have rollback steps ready.

alex: TL;DR: experiment window 45m tomorrow 02:00 UTC, temporary internal SLO relaxation p99 120->220ms for /v1/generate on canary pool, monitoring + runbook posted, oncall + infra watching. Ping me or @jamal if you see anything. :rocket:
